```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6)
```

## 1. Data

```{r data}
library(mgcv)
aq <- na.omit(airquality[, c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")])
y  <- log(aq$Ozone)
xs <- aq[, c("Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")]
n  <- length(y); p <- ncol(xs)
```

## 2. Backfitting with smoothing splines (3 df each)

Model: $y_i = \beta_0 + \sum_j f_j(x_{ij}) + \varepsilon_i$ with
$\sum_i f_j(x_{ij}) = 0$. The intercept is $\hat\beta_0 = \bar y$ and is
kept in every partial residual. After each update the new $f_j$ is centred.

```{r backfit}
beta0 <- mean(y)
f <- matrix(0, n, p, dimnames = list(NULL, names(xs)))
for (it in 1:50) {
  f_old <- f
  for (j in 1:p) {
    r  <- y - beta0 - rowSums(f[, -j, drop = FALSE])   # partial residual
    sj <- smooth.spline(xs[[j]], r, df = 3)
    fj <- predict(sj, xs[[j]])$y
    f[, j] <- fj - mean(fj)                            # centring
  }
  if (max(abs(f - f_old)) < 1e-8) break
}
c(iterations = it, beta0 = beta0)
round(colMeans(f), 12)    # every component has mean zero
```

## 3. Backfitting with the smoothers of an `mgcv` fit reproduces `gam()`

For fixed smoothing parameters, the penalized least-squares estimates solve
$f_j = A_j\,(y - \beta_0\mathbf 1 - \sum_{k\ne j} f_k)$ with
$A_j = X_j(X_j^\top X_j + \lambda_j S_j)^{-1}X_j^\top$.
Backfitting is Gauss–Seidel on these equations, so it must converge to the
`gam()` solution.

```{r exact}
g  <- gam(log(Ozone) ~ s(Solar.R) + s(Wind) + s(Temp), data = aq, method = "REML")
X  <- model.matrix(g)
round(colSums(X)[2:4], 10)          # mgcv's constrained columns sum to zero
A  <- lapply(seq_along(g$smooth), function(j) {
  sm <- g$smooth[[j]]; ii <- sm$first.para:sm$last.para
  Xj <- X[, ii]
  Xj %*% solve(crossprod(Xj) + g$sp[j] * sm$S[[1]], t(Xj))
})
f2 <- matrix(0, n, p); b0 <- mean(y)
for (it in 1:500) {
  f_old <- f2
  for (j in 1:p) f2[, j] <- A[[j]] %*% (y - b0 - rowSums(f2[, -j, drop = FALSE]))
  if (max(abs(f2 - f_old)) < 1e-10) break
}
tm <- predict(g, type = "terms")
c(iterations = it, max_abs_diff = max(abs(f2 - tm)), intercept_diff = b0 - coef(g)[[1]])
```

## 4. Compare the shapes

```{r plot}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (j in 1:p) {
  o <- order(xs[[j]])
  plot(xs[[j]][o], tm[o, j], type = "l", lwd = 2, xlab = names(xs)[j],
       ylab = "centred effect", ylim = range(tm, f))
  lines(xs[[j]][o], f[o, j], col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
}
legend("topleft", c("gam (REML)", "backfit, 3 df"), col = c("black", "red"),
       lty = 1:2, bty = "n")
```

The smoothing-spline version uses a different amount of smoothing (3 df
per term), so the curves differ a little; the exact version agrees with
`gam()` to about $10^{-11}$.
